result.markdown: --- title: "Week 12: LVPA Identification & Fit" date: today description: 'Download PDF' format: revealjs: theme: simple slide-number: true embed-resources: true self-contained-math: true --- # Agenda - Global Fit Review - Assumptions - The 2-step workflow - Examples - Rlab ## Review Lamaku > quizzes > W12 Global fit indices 8 min (2 min / question) ## What do we already know? {.smaller} | | **MVPA (Weeks 3-6)** | **CFA (Weeks 7-10)** | |:--|:--|:--| | **Models** | Paths among **measured** variables | Indicators reflecting **latent** variables | | **Identification** | df ≥ 0, recursive model | adds Scale, 3-indicator rule | | **Fit** | χ², CFI, RMSEA, SRMR | Same indices; residuals | | **Key results** | Direct, indirect, total effects | Loadings, residual variances, AVE, reliability | | **Report** | Standardized & unstandardized | same | | **Interpret** | Relationships between measured variables | convergent & discriminant validity | ## LVPA Assumptions Check these before fitting - Correct specification: theory-based - Identification: df ≥ 0, every latent variable has a scale, enough indicators per latent variable - Adequate sample size: ≥ 10 cases per parameter - Continuous, multivariate normal indicators (or use MLR / DWLS for ordinal) - Linear relationships - Missing data MCAR or MAR (FIML) - Independent observations ## Pisa Data - extended {.smaller} | Variable | What it measures | Indicators | Response scale | |:--|:--|:-:|:--| | Growth Mindset (`Growth.Mind`, latent) | Belief that ability can be developed, rather than being fixed | 4 | 4-point agreement | | Stress Resilience (`Stress.Res`, latent) | Ability to stay calm and cope when under pressure | 10 | 5-point | | Math Anxiety (`Math.Anx`, latent) | Worry, tension and helplessness about math | 6 | 4-point agreement | | Math Score (`Math.Sc`, observed) | Math achievement | 1 | continuous (÷ 100) | ## Research Design Notes 1. Students don't all see the same items. 2. Sections can be absent by country. 3. "Missing" has different meanings: not administered (by design) & non-response (all treated as NA). 4. Some students have no questionnaire data (about 1,900 of GBR's 12,972): removed. 5. Plausible values: we average them; for publication, run a model of each one and pool the results. ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.notes} The pairwise coverage was uneven but adequate: the thinnest pair of Stress.Res items was observed together for about 18% of the full GBR sample. Run `lavInspect(fit, "coverage")` to show students. The slides use a random sample of 1,000 students from the 11,037 who answered at least one item. ::: ::: ## Pisa Data - extended {.smaller} PISA 2022, Great Britain: a **random sample of *N* = 1000** students (seeded; from 11,037 who answered at least one item). | Assumption | Our data | |:--|:--| | Sample size | 1000 vs. ~40-50 parameters: fine | | Continuous & normal | 4- and 5-point Likert items. **MLR** (robust SEs and χ²) | | Missing data | Missing MCAR - use **FIML** | | Independence | One response / student | ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.notes} Missing codes 7, 8, 9, 95, 97, 98, 99 were recoded to NA in the data-prep script (rlabs/pisa_data_wrangle_anx_stress_growth.R); the ~1,900 students with no questionnaire data were removed. USA is not used because Stress.Res was not administered there (all 97). ::: ::: ## Pisa Data - extended {.smaller} - **Math.Anx (6 items):** higher = more anxious (reversed from the raw file) - **Growth.Mind (4 items):** higher = stronger Growth.Mind (reversed from the raw file) - **Stress.Res (10 items):** higher = more resilient (same as raw file) - **Math.Sc:** mean of 10 plausible values, divided by 100 ## The two-step workflow 1. Measurement model first: - Identification → global fit → local fit → (modify) → interpret - If it fits poorly, no structural result is trustworthy. 2. Then add structure - Identification → global fit → local fit → interpret ## Identification checklist {.smaller} | Rule | From | Why | |:--|:--|:--| | df ≥ 0 | MVPA | Can't estimate more than the information supplies | | Every latent variable has a scale (marker or fixed variance) | CFA | Otherwise infinitely many solutions | | ≥ 3 indicators per factor | CFA | Smallest just-identified one-factor model | | Recursive structural model | MVPA | Always identified if measurement is | Information = p(p + 1) / 2, p = number of measured variables. Latent variables add none. # Ex 1: **RQ:** Do students higher in Stress.Res report *lower Math.Anx*, and is lower Math.Anx associated with *higher Math.Sc*? ## The model ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w12_LVPA_identification_fit_report_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1248} ::: ::: *N* = 1000 (random sample); items treated as continuous; MLR + FIML. ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.notes} Math.Sc is a single observed variable (mean of plausible values). It is not a latent variable, so it has no loadings. Its variance is a free parameter in the measurement model. ::: ::: ## Ex 1: Measurement model diagram ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w12_LVPA_identification_fit_report_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1440} ::: ::: Curved orange arrows = covariances among the latent variables and Math.Sc (no directional paths); ε = residual variances; the first loading of each factor is fixed to 1. ## Ex 1: Measurement model: information Work out for the measurement model: the **measured variables**, the pieces of **information** we have. ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} Measured variables: 10 Stress.Res + 6 Math.Anx + 1 Math.Sc = **17** Information: 17(18)/2 = **153** ::: ::: ## Ex 1: Parameters Used {.smaller} Now determine the **free parameters (q)**, and the **df**. ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} | Type | Count | |:--|:-:| | Loadings (after fixing one marker per factor) | 9 + 5 = 14 | | Residual variances of indicators (θ) | 16 | | Variances of latent variables (Stress.Res, Math.Anx) | 2 | | Variance of Math.Sc | 1 | | Covariances: Stress.Res↔ Math.Anx, Stress.Res↔ Math.Sc, Math.Anx↔ Math.Sc | 3 | q = 14 + 16 + 2 + 1 + 3 = **36**; df = 153 − 36 = **117**. Over-identified. ::: ::: ## Ex 1: Specify {.smaller} ```r meas_model <- ' # measurement model stress =~ str1 + str2 + str3 + str4 + str5 + str6 + str7 + str8 + str9 + str10 anx =~ anx1 + anx2 + anx3 + anx4 + anx5 + anx6 # observed math score covaries with each factor math ~~ stress + anx stress ~~ anx ' ``` - `=~` measured by; the first loading is fixed to 1 by default (marker). - `~~` between two variables is a **covariance**: `stress ~~ anx` makes explicit that the two factors covary (no direction). - `math ~~ stress + anx`: Math.Sc is observed & covaries with each factor. - We must include all indicators/latent vars that will be in the structure model ## Ex 1: Global fit {.smaller} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Index | Value| |:--------------|--------------:| |χ² (scaled) | 556.52| |df | 117| |p | < .001| |CFI (robust) | 0.854| |TLI (robust) | 0.830| |RMSEA (robust) | 0.109| |90% CI | [0.098, 0.121]| |SRMR | 0.072| ::: ::: ## Practice: Evaluate how good the fit is ## Ex 1: Local fit: modification indices ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |lhs | |rhs | MI| EPC| std EPC| |:----|:--|:----|------:|-----:|-------:| |anx5 |~~ |anx6 | 164.46| 0.24| 0.61| |str3 |~~ |str6 | 40.99| -0.39| -0.55| |str6 |~~ |str9 | 37.21| 0.36| 0.55| |anx3 |~~ |anx4 | 29.99| 0.06| 0.39| |str3 |~~ |str7 | 29.29| 0.40| 0.43| |str1 |~~ |str3 | 27.30| 0.35| 0.45| |str3 |~~ |str5 | 26.35| -0.33| -0.42| |str5 |~~ |str6 | 24.03| 0.29| 0.43| ::: ::: - MI = expected χ² drop (1 df) if that residual covariance were freed. - MI > 3.84 is "significant", but with *N* = 1000 nearly everything is. - Look for **big** and **explainable**: same factor, same wording, adjacent items. ## Ex 1: Modify one at a time - Free the largest **defensible** residual covariance, refit, recheck MIs. - Step = free the parameter, rerun the model, rerun the fit indices, rerun the MI. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | Step|Freed | MI| CFI| RMSEA| SRMR| |----:|:------------|---:|-----:|-----:|-----:| | 0|none | | 0.854| 0.109| 0.072| | 1|anx5 ~~ anx6 | 164| 0.892| 0.094| 0.071| | 2|str6 ~~ str9 | 37| 0.923| 0.080| 0.070| | 3|str5 ~~ str6 | 26| 0.927| 0.078| 0.069| ::: ::: ## Ex 1: Final measurement model: diagram ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w12_LVPA_identification_fit_report_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1536} ::: ::: Standardized estimates. Curved double-headed arrows = covariances (correlations) among Stress.Res, Math.Anx and Math.Sc; loops = residual variances; the short arrows between neighbouring items are the three residual covariances. Negative estimates in red. ## Ex 1: Final measurement model: diagram (labelled version) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: The `label.size` argument of `geom_label()` is deprecated as of ggplot2 3.5.0. ℹ Please use the `linewidth` argument instead. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w12_LVPA_identification_fit_report_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1440} ::: ::: - Standardized estimates. ## Ex 1: Final measurement model fit {.smaller} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Model | df| χ²| CFI| RMSEA| SRMR| |:------------------------|---:|------:|-----:|-----:|-----:| |Initial | 117| 556.52| 0.854| 0.109| 0.072| |+ 3 residual covariances | 114| 347.96| 0.927| 0.078| 0.069| ::: ::: - Now df = 114 (three more parameters). - CFI = 0.927 (acceptable), RMSEA = 0.078 (acceptable), SRMR = 0.069 (acceptable). - All three are in the acceptable (although not "good") range, so we can proceed to the structure model. ## Ex 1: Measurement model: Interpret {.smaller} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Factor |Item | b| β| Resid. var| |:----------|:-----|----:|----:|----------:| |Stress.Res |str1 | 1.00| 0.77| 0.40| |Stress.Res |str2 | 0.53| 0.45| 0.80| |Stress.Res |str3 | 0.85| 0.69| 0.53| |Stress.Res |str4 | 1.12| 0.87| 0.25| |Stress.Res |str5 | 0.58| 0.51| 0.74| |Stress.Res |str6 | 0.81| 0.66| 0.57| |Stress.Res |str7 | 0.76| 0.59| 0.65| |Stress.Res |str8 | 0.61| 0.52| 0.73| |Stress.Res |str9 | 0.80| 0.63| 0.60| |Stress.Res |str10 | 0.82| 0.69| 0.53| |Math.Anx |anx1 | 1.00| 0.80| 0.35| |Math.Anx |anx2 | 1.02| 0.83| 0.31| |Math.Anx |anx3 | 1.07| 0.90| 0.19| |Math.Anx |anx4 | 1.07| 0.88| 0.22| |Math.Anx |anx5 | 0.96| 0.73| 0.46| |Math.Anx |anx6 | 0.95| 0.69| 0.52| ::: ::: ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} - Standardized loadings ranged from 0.45 to 0.90. Math.Anx items load strongly (about .7-.9); Stress.Res items are more mixed. These are *standardized*: SD change in the item per SD of the factor. ::: ## Practice How do you interpret these loadings? ## Ex 1: Factor relationships {.smaller} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Pair | r| 95% CI lower| 95% CI upper| |:---------------------|-----:|------------:|------------:| |Stress.Res ↔ Math.Sc | 0.12| 0.04| 0.19| |Math.Anx ↔ Math.Sc | -0.36| -0.42| -0.30| |Stress.Res ↔ Math.Anx | -0.42| -0.50| -0.34| ::: ::: Practice: How do you interpret the factor correlations? ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} - **Discriminant validity:** Moderate correlations between Stress.Res and Math.Anx, suggesting distinct constructs. - Signs match theory? Negative relationship between Stress.Res ↔ Math.Anx is expected - *Observed* Math.Sc ↔ latent correlations are also weak/moderate ::: ::: ## Ex 1 structure model ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w12_LVPA_identification_fit_report_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1152} ::: ::: - Structural part only - The indicators and their loadings are unchanged from the measurement model (not drawn). ## Ex 1: Structural model, identification {.smaller} Start from the measurement model (q = 39, df = 114) and determine this changes the identification. ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} | Change | Parameters | |:--|:-:| | Remove covariances Stress.Res↔ Math.Anx, Stress.Res↔ Math.Sc, Math.Anx↔ Math.Sc | −3 | | Add paths a (Stress.Res → Math.Anx) and b (Math.Anx → Math.Sc) | +2 | | Variances of Math.Anx and Math.Sc become **disturbances** (still free, same count) | 0 | ::: ::: ## Pause: Practice 1. What does the structural model theorize about the Stress.Res, math.anx, and Math.Sc relationship? ## Ex 1: Structural model: Specify {.smaller} ```r sem_model <- ' # measurement model (same as Step 1) stress =~ str1 + str2 + str3 + str4 + str5 + str6 + str7 + str8 + str9 + str10 anx =~ anx1 + anx2 + anx3 + anx4 + anx5 + anx6 # residual covariances freed in Step 1 anx5 ~~ anx6 str6 ~~ str9 str5 ~~ str6 # structural paths (replace the covariances among stress, anx, math) anx ~ a*stress math ~ b*anx # indirect effect ind := a*b ' ``` - `~` is a regression; `a*`, `b*` label paths; `:=` defines the indirect effect. - The residual covariances from Step 1 **stay in**: the measurement model doesn't change. ## Ex 1: Global fit ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Model | df| χ²| CFI| RMSEA| SRMR| |:-----------|---:|------:|-----:|-----:|-----:| |Measurement | 114| 347.96| 0.927| 0.078| 0.069| |Structural | 115| 348.87| 0.927| 0.078| 0.069| ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: Scaled Δχ²(1) = 1.05, *p* = 0.306 ::: {.fragment} - A **significant** Δχ² would mean the structural model fits worse than the measurement model (non-sig: not worse - good) - Also look at the *change in CFI and RMSEA* (here, essentially none). ::: ## Ex 1: Local fit: MI (opt) ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |lhs | |rhs | MI| EPC| std EPC| |:----------|:--|:----------|----:|-----:|-------:| |Math.Anx |~ |Math.Sc | 1.24| -0.08| -0.10| |Stress.Res |~ |Math.Sc | 1.24| -0.05| -0.05| |Math.Sc |~ |Stress.Res | 1.24| -0.04| -0.04| ::: ::: - Look for omitted **paths** (`~`), not just residual covariances. - Compare with the Δχ² result: the only structural thing the model leaves out is `math ~ stress`. - Don't add it just because MI says so: it must make **theoretical** sense. ## Ex 1: Interpret: path coefficients diagram ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w12_LVPA_identification_fit_report_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1536} ::: ::: - Standardized estimates (β). - Residual variances and the three residual covariances from Step 1 are modeled but not drawn due to space. ## Ex 1: Interpret: path {.smaller} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Effect | b| SE| p| β| |:-----------------------------------------|------:|-----:|------:|------:| |Stress.Res → Math.Anx | -0.317| 0.038| < .001| -0.421| |Math.Anx → Math.Sc | -0.453| 0.045| < .001| -0.357| |Indirect: Stress.Res → Math.Anx → Math.Sc | 0.144| 0.022| < .001| 0.150| ::: ::: - β is the standardized result, but we report both. - Indirect effect `ind` = a·b. Its CI should be **bootstrapped**. ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.notes} - Students higher in Stress.Res reported **lower** Math.Anx (*b* = -0.32, β = -0.42). - Higher Math.Anx was associated with **lower** Math.Sc (*b* = -0.45, i.e. 45.29 points per unit, β = -0.36). - Indirect effect β = 0.15: positive and small. Both paths are negative, so the product is positive (higher Stress.Res → lower Math.Anx → higher Math.Sc), and it is small because it multiplies two modest numbers. - Associations only: cross-sectional, so "affects" is not supported by these data alone. ::: ::: ## Ex 1: Interpret: R² ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Variable | R²| |:-----------------|----:| |Math.Anx (latent) | 0.18| |Math.Sc | 0.13| ::: ::: - R² = share of variance explained by predictors; the rest is the disturbance. - Is 0.13 meaningful for Math.Sc in education research? # Example 2 **RQ:** Does Growth.Mind relate to lower Math.Anx *directly* and *through* Stress.Res, and does Math.Anx carry the link to Math.Sc? ## Ex 2: The model ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w12_LVPA_identification_fit_report_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1536} ::: ::: ## Ex 2: Measurement model: Specify Write the `lavaan` syntax for the **measurement model**: which latent variables, which indicators, and how is Math.Sc handled? ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} ```r meas_model2 <- ' gm =~ gm1 + gm2 + gm3 + gm4 stress =~ str1 + str2 + str3 + str4 + str5 + str6 + str7 + str8 + str9 + str10 anx =~ anx1 + anx2 + anx3 + anx4 + anx5 + anx6 math ~~ gm + stress + anx ' fit_meas2 <- cfa(meas_model2, data = pisa, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml") ``` ::: ::: ## Ex 2: Measurement model: Identification Count the **measured variables**, the **information**, the **free parameters (q)** and the **df**. ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} Measured variables: 4 + 10 + 6 + 1 = **21**; information = 21(22)/2 = **231** ::: ::: {.fragment} Loadings 3 + 9 + 5 = 17; residual variances 20; latent variances 3; Math.Sc variance 1; covariances 3 + 3 = 6. ::: ::: {.fragment} q = 47; df = 231 − 47 = **184**. ::: ::: ## Ex 2: Measurement model: Global fit ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Index | Value| |:--------------|--------------:| |χ² (scaled) | 771.11| |df | 184| |p | < .001| |CFI (robust) | 0.860| |TLI (robust) | 0.840| |RMSEA (robust) | 0.093| |90% CI | [0.085, 0.102]| |SRMR | 0.069| ::: ::: ## Ex 2: Measurement model: Global fit Is the global fit acceptable? ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} No: CFI is well below .90 and RMSEA is above .08. Poor. ::: ::: ## Ex 2: Modification Indices {.smaller} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |lhs | |rhs | MI| EPC| std EPC| |:----|:--|:----|------:|-----:|-------:| |anx5 |~~ |anx6 | 163.65| 0.24| 0.61| |gm2 |~~ |gm3 | 119.99| 0.65| 5.60| |gm1 |~~ |gm4 | 75.50| 0.14| 0.29| |str3 |~~ |str6 | 41.11| -0.39| -0.56| |str6 |~~ |str9 | 37.55| 0.36| 0.55| |anx3 |~~ |anx4 | 29.80| 0.06| 0.38| |str3 |~~ |str7 | 29.20| 0.40| 0.43| |str1 |~~ |str3 | 27.60| 0.35| 0.46| ::: ::: Which modification indices would you consider, and are they defensible? ## Ex 2: Modify one at a time - Same procedure as Ex 1: free the largest **defensible** residual covariance, refit, recheck MIs. - Step = free the parameter, rerun the model, rerun the fit indices, rerun the MI. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | Step|Freed | MI| CFI| RMSEA| SRMR| |----:|:------------|---:|-----:|-----:|-----:| | 0|none | | 0.860| 0.093| 0.069| | 1|anx5 ~~ anx6 | 164| 0.892| 0.082| 0.068| | 2|str6 ~~ str9 | 37| 0.916| 0.073| 0.068| | 3|str5 ~~ str6 | 25| 0.920| 0.071| 0.067| ::: ::: ## Ex 2: Measurement model: Modify ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Model | df| χ²| CFI| RMSEA| SRMR| |:------------------------|---:|------:|-----:|-----:|-----:| |Initial | 184| 771.11| 0.860| 0.093| 0.069| |+ 3 residual covariances | 181| 562.92| 0.920| 0.071| 0.067| ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | Step|Freed | Δχ² (1 df)| p| Estimate| Sign | |----:|:------------|----------:|------:|--------:|:----:| | 1|anx5 ~~ anx6 | 44.59| < .001| 0.26| + | | 2|str6 ~~ str9 | 22.76| < .001| 0.42| + | | 3|str5 ~~ str6 | 8.60| 0.003| 0.28| + | ::: ::: Is the fit now acceptable enough to move on? ## Ex 2: Measurement model: Interpret ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w12_LVPA_identification_fit_report_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-25-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1536} ::: ::: - Standardized estimates - Residual variances and the three residual covariances are in the model but not drawn. ## Ex 2: Measurement model: Interpret (relationships) {.smaller} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Covariance | b| SE| z| p| β| |:------------------------|------:|-----:|------:|------:|------:| |Growth.Mind ↔ Math.Sc | 0.057| 0.013| 4.248| < .001| 0.159| |Stress.Res ↔ Math.Sc | 0.099| 0.033| 3.040| 0.002| 0.115| |Math.Anx ↔ Math.Sc | -0.231| 0.025| -9.383| < .001| -0.358| |Growth.Mind ↔ Stress.Res | 0.056| 0.016| 3.446| < .001| 0.150| |Growth.Mind ↔ Math.Anx | -0.064| 0.013| -4.998| < .001| -0.228| |Stress.Res ↔ Math.Anx | -0.286| 0.031| -9.308| < .001| -0.423| ::: ::: b = covariance; β = standardized covariance (the correlation). 1. Do the signs match theory? 2. Is there evidence of discriminant validity? Which factor is the weakest measure? ## Ex 2: Structural model: Specify {.smaller} Write the `lavaan` syntax for the **structural model** (keep the measurement part and the residual covariances from above). Name the paths and define the indirect effects of interest. ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} ```r sem_model2 <- ' gm =~ gm1 + gm2 + gm3 + gm4 stress =~ str1 + str2 + str3 + str4 + str5 + str6 + str7 + str8 + str9 + str10 anx =~ anx1 + anx2 + anx3 + anx4 + anx5 + anx6 anx5 ~~ anx6 str6 ~~ str9 str5 ~~ str6 stress ~ g1*gm anx ~ g2*gm + s*stress math ~ b*anx ind_gm_stress_anx := g1*s ind_gm_anx_math := (g2 + g1*s)*b ' fit_sem2 <- sem(sem_model2, data = pisa, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml") ``` ::: ::: ## Ex 2: Structural model: Identification {.smaller} Starting from the measurement model (q = 50, df = 181), how does DF change? which parameters are replaced? What are q and df now? ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} - Remove the 6 covariances (3 among the latents, 3 with Math.Sc); - add 4 paths (gm → stress, gm → anx, stress → anx, anx → math); the variances of stress, anx and Math.Sc become disturbances (same count). - q = 50 − 6 + 4 = **48**; df = 231 − 48 = **183**. ::: ::: ## Ex 2: Structural model: Fit ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Model | df| χ²| CFI| RMSEA| SRMR| |:-----------------------|---:|------:|-----:|-----:|-----:| |Measurement (saturated) | 181| 562.92| 0.920| 0.071| 0.067| |Structural | 183| 569.97| 0.919| 0.071| 0.068| ::: ::: ## Ex 2: Modification Indices ::: {.cell} ::: Scaled Δχ²(2) = 7.10, *p* = 0.029 ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |lhs | |rhs | MI| EPC| std EPC| |:-----------|:--|:-----------|----:|-----:|-------:| |Growth.Mind |~ |Math.Sc | 6.13| 0.04| 0.09| |Math.Sc |~ |Growth.Mind | 6.13| 0.18| 0.08| |Stress.Res |~ |Math.Sc | 2.34| -0.07| -0.07| |Math.Sc |~ |Stress.Res | 1.22| -0.04| -0.04| |Math.Anx |~ |Math.Sc | 0.02| 0.01| 0.01| ::: ::: ::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"} ::: {.fragment} The Δχ² tests the two omitted paths together. It is significant at .05, but CFI and RMSEA barely change. The largest MI for an omitted path is Growth.Mind ↔ Math.Sc (about 6), small. Is a direct Growth.Mind → Math.Sc path theoretically sensible?
